title: 1951 AHSME Problem 37
statement: A number which when divided by \(10\) leaves a remainder of \(9,\) when divided by \(9\) leaves a remainder of \(8,\) by \(8\) leaves a remainder of \(7,\) etc., down to where, when divided by \(2,\) it leaves a remainder of \(1,\) is:

solutions.text:
If the number is \(N,\) then \(N+1\) is divisible by every integer from \(2\) through \(10.\) Their least common multiple is \[ 2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5\cdot7=2520. \] Thus the least positive number fitting all the conditions is \(N=2520-1=2519.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Adding \(1\) to the desired number removes every listed remainder
